<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to find which option is NOT part of the U.S. national COVID-19 preparedness plan. We read the plan: It's a long document summarizing goals: protect and treat, monitor variants, maintain supply, etc. They mention: "Prevent Economic and Educational Shutdowns" and "Continue to Lead the Effort to Vaccinate the World and Save Lives" – global aspects. Let's analyze each option:

A. "With insufficient tools to fight COVID-19, the United States mobilized all of society to insist on surviving the outbreak with the least disruption to the United States." This is narrative; But does the plan say "mobilized all of society to insist on surviving the outbreak with the least disruption"? The plan mentions "whole-of-society effort" and "all-of-society." For example, earlier in the "Protect Against and Treat COVID-19" section: "The Administration has put vaccines at the center... The Administration has mobilized an unprecedented, whole-of-society effort to give Americans the tools they need to protect themselves." Also: "The path forward is clear: schools, workers, and workplaces have resources and guidance to prevent shutdowns." So Option A likely part of the plan.

But wording: "mobilized all of society to insist on surviving the outbreak with the least disruption" - maybe not exactly a core component? However seems generically true. It might still be part of the plan: the whole-of-society included vaccines, etc. So likely A is part.

B. "Minimize the impact of new variants on the United States by collecting and analyzing data on previous variants of COVID-19 and strengthening regulation and review of specific variants." That is indeed part of the plan: variant monitoring, data collection, sequencing, and regulatory review to expedite variant-specific vaccines. So B is part.

C. "Take specific measures for businesses and schools to help businesses and schools continue to operate through COVID-19 to reduce the cost and impact of the pandemic on the U.S. economy." This is part of "Prevent Economic and Educational Shutdowns" section. Yes. That is part of plan.

D. "Expand global access to COVID-19 medicines, facilitate the formation of pharmaceutical research alliances, and increase global funding." The national COVID-19 preparedness plan: While the plan is national, it may include global aspects to prevent variants? The plan as described had global: "At the start we expanded global access to medicines" but the question: "Which of the following options is not part of the U.S. national COVID-19 preparedness plan?" Might be including global component is not part of the national plan? I recall that the national plan primarily focuses on U.S. domestic readiness. But some of the document like "Continue to Lead the Effort to Vaccinate the World and Save Lives" might be considered as part of national plan? But the national plan may include some global actions: "To ensure that people stay protected, the U.S. government will increase American manufacturing capacity to reliably produce an additional 1 billion vaccine doses per year – and the plan will include export provisions." However the national plan maybe separate from global vaccine donation commitments, which are in separate sections maybe not part of the national plan. The question: Which option is NOT part of the national plan? Option D: expand global access to medicines, facilitate formation of research alliances, increase global funding. That seems more like global initiatives; Not part of national plan.

Thus answer is D. Let's confirm: The plan includes "Prevent Economic and Educational Shutdowns," "Prepare for New Variants," "Strengthen Supply," "Develop Safe Home Testing," etc. It also includes "Continue to Lead the Effort to Vaccinate the World and Save Lives." But maybe that section is part of national plan? Let's search. In the above transcript, after the national plan, after "Prevent Economic and Educational Shutdowns", there's a section "Continue to Lead the Effort to Vaccinate the World and Save Lives." That appears to be part of the broader plan (international). But the original question: "Which of the following options is not part of the U.S. national COVID-19 preparedness plan?" The plan as described includes domestic measures and also global efforts. But maybe the national plan refers only to U.S. internal policy. The global actions may be considered part of "global health" policy, not national plan. The question likely expects D.

Hence answer: \boxed{D}.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>\boxed{D}
